editorial:
Imagine a movie that plays with your head by showing you one woman through four different lenses. You get to see a variety of female characters who all represent different sides of the same person, and it creates a really interesting vibe. It is a mix of drama and comedy that feels very grounded in the early 80s. You will find yourself wondering which version of the character is the real one as the story unfolds and the men in her life react to these different personalities. It is a quirky take on identity that keeps you guessing without being too confusing.

The acting is the real star here because the performers have to switch moods and styles quickly. While the pacing can feel a bit slow in the middle, the weirdness of the setup makes it worth your time. If you like indie films that experiment with how a story is told, you should definitely give this a go. Since it is an older gem, you might want to track down a high-quality 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the detail, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night.
endingExplained: At the end, the different versions of the woman merge into a single realization about her life. You see that the four characters were not separate people, but different masks she wore to survive her relationships with men. The movie wraps up by showing her finally accepting all these parts of herself. Instead of being split apart, she finds a sense of peace and independence, leaving the men behind to start her own fresh chapter.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological character studies and old European cinema.
